meta.title: OpenKortex · the second brain you host yourself
meta.description: Drop web pages, PDFs, videos, voice memos and meetings into one inbox. OpenKortex summarizes, tags and links them with your own AI keys and keeps everything as plain Markdown on your server. Open source under AGPL-3.0.
nav.label: Main
hero.title: Drop it in. Find it sorted.
hero.lead: OpenKortex is a second brain you run yourself. Web pages, e-books, recipes, photos, voice memos, meetings and prompts land in one inbox. Your own AI keys turn them into summaries, tags and links, kept as plain Markdown on your server.
hero.note: The demo runs in your browser with sample data. No account, no server, no AI.
orbit.label: Every app sends what you capture to your OpenKortex server, which files it as Markdown in your folder and answers your AI agents.
principles.label: Principles
p1.title: Your notes are files.
p1.text: Every entry is Markdown with YAML frontmatter, mirrored to a folder on your computer. Open it in any editor, today or in twenty years.
p2.title: Your server, your keys.
p2.text: There is no OpenKortex cloud. It runs where you install it and only calls the AI providers you give a key to.
p3.title: Your agents are welcome.
p3.text: A built-in MCP server lets Claude and other agents search, read and save, with a token you can revoke at any time.
flow.title: From drop to answer
flow.lead: What happens after you press capture.
s1.title: Capture
s1.text: Share from your phone, clip in the browser, press Alt+Space on Windows or let the meeting recorder listen. It all lands in one inbox.
s2.title: Sort
s2.text: In the background, OpenKortex transcribes, summarizes and pulls out tasks and people. Each entry gets tags and a folder. What you placed by hand stays put.
s3.title: Connect
s3.text: Wiki links, backlinks and objects for people, projects and ideas tie entries together. The graph shows what belongs with what.
s4.title: Ask
s4.text: Ask in your own words. The copilot answers from your notes and shows every source it used.
ui.sum1: Local-first apps keep data on your devices and sync in the background.
ui.sum2: CRDTs merge edits without a central server deciding who wins.
ui.task: Try CRDT sync in the Atlas project
ui.q: What did I save about sync conflicts?
ui.a: Two things. The local-first talk recommends CRDTs, so edits merge on their own. Your Atlas notes go another way: keep a .conflict.md copy instead of overwriting.

apps.title: One brain, every way in
apps.lead: Your server holds your knowledge. Each app is a door to it and asks for your server's address on first start.
apps.webText: Today screen, block editor with wiki links and backlinks, journal, graph, search by meaning.
apps.windowsText: Quick capture with Alt+Space, and meeting notes that record microphone and system audio without a bot.
apps.extensionText: Clip pages, highlight text, manage tabs and export chats with AI assistants.
apps.mcpText: Six tools for Claude and other agents: search, read, save, organize, tasks and memory.
apps.mdText: Two-way sync with a local folder of plain .md files, ready for Obsidian or any editor.
selfhost.title: Your own server in one command
selfhost.lead: OpenKortex comes as one Docker Compose stack: the web app, the MCP server, Supabase with Postgres and pgvector, and a gateway that gets the https certificate for you.
selfhost.need2: One AI key: Anthropic, OpenRouter or Eden AI
selfhost.need3: A domain, if you want to use it from your phone
selfhost.key: add an AI key to selfhost/.env, then

apps.mobileText: Share sheet, push-to-talk voice memos, photos, editor and chat. Android today; iOS is prepared in the code.
soon.title: Not public yet
soon.lead: The OpenKortex source code is being prepared for its public release under the AGPL-3.0. The repository, the self-hosting guide and the contribution rules will open here on the day it goes public.
soon.meanwhile: Until then, the live demo shows the whole app in your browser.
